raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

For rejection sampling, EAGLE, NEXTN, UNO and DFLASH call this sampler eagerly. DSpark does too, unless `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH` (off by default) captures the accept step in a CUDA graph. With `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION=1`, that graph uses blockwise rejection unless block verification is on.

On `main`, one GPU program per request walks the vocabulary for the final token. For a final coin within about 16 FP32 steps of 1 (about 1e-6 of draws), `main` can return a zero-weight or out-of-vocabulary token.

## Modifications

Above 32,768 tokens, the final draw sums weights in parallel over 4,096-token blocks, then scans one block. Up to 32,768 tokens, the draw stays in the acceptance kernel, with 8 warps above a 4,096-lane tile. The draw returns a positive-weight token when the residual has one. Existing configs need no change.

## Accuracy Tests

The empty-residual fallback matches `main` ([concrete inputs](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44116#issuecomment-6548458208)). The cutoff test fails on `main`. The sparse test passes there and fails here without either residual filter.

```text
Sampler on B200, main -> PR
62,080 draws: acceptance matched, 39 final tokens differed, all at CDF boundaries
1,043,200 draws with coins just below 1: out-of-vocabulary 5,294 -> 0, zero-weight 2,801 -> 0

GSM8K, main -> PR
Qwen3.5-9B, TP2, test_eagle_reject_sampling (run_eval, 200 examples): 0.905 -> 0.91
GLM-5.3-Flash on a7f21b74aa merged with c108a656f1, one run per arm, sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max tokens 32768, thinking: 97.50 -> 98.50 (2 questions, no gain claimed)
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The table shows median µs for token-wise verification at batch 4. The Graph columns need `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH`.

| Vocabulary | Eager: main | Eager: PR | Graph: main | Graph: PR |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | 31.50 | 31.21 | 6.26 | 6.25 |
| 8,193 | 33.59 | 31.40 | 12.42 | 10.34 |
| 32,000 | 41.82 | 35.92 | 20.60 | 14.47 |
| 32,001 | 48.25 | 53.96 | 26.77 | 32.88 |
| 50,257 | 71.72 | 63.99 | 51.30 | 10.35 |
| 65,536 | 57.85 | 61.86 | 36.98 | 10.34 |
| 128,256 | 80.75 | 61.97 | 59.51 | 10.38 |
| 154,880 | 88.32 | 63.26 | 65.70 | 10.38 |

Serving showed no clear change.

```text
Eager time as a ratio of main
Both modes, batches 4 and 48:  32,001 1.11-1.16x   32,769 1.19-1.32x   50,257 0.89-1.04x   65,536 1.05-1.14x   100,000 0.80-0.95x
Token-wise, batch 256, 1024:   32,000 1.17x, 1.32x   32,001 2.19x, 3.23x

Graph time as a ratio of main
Token-wise, batch 256, 1024:   32,000 1.33x, 1.40x   32,001 2.83x, 3.73x

Serving, main -> PR
NEXTN rejection sampling, one GPU, three alternating rounds, tok/s range
TinyLlama-1.1B (32,000)      sequential 906-916 -> 911-919     256 concurrent 55,270-57,721 -> 55,654-58,961
OpenHermes-2.5-7B (32,002)   sequential 280-282 -> 279-283     256 concurrent 14,986-15,984 -> 15,549-15,726

GLM-5.3-Flash (154,880), TP4, EAGLE 5 steps, top-k 1, one run per arm on a7f21b74aa merged with c108a656f1, before the inline limit moved to 32,768
cold concurrency 1      525.76 -> 513.08 tok/s, ITL 1.38 -> 1.43 ms
warm concurrency 1      524.27 -> 525.21 tok/s, ITL 1.43 -> 1.41 ms
concurrency 16          1175.55 -> 1221.18 tok/s, ITL 6.80 -> 5.64 ms, mean TTFT 1605.67 -> 1817.03 ms
prefill concurrency 16  45.84 -> 46.08 tok/s
```

<details>
<summary>Timing script</summary>

```python
"""Usage from the repository root: python speed.py BASELINE_FILE VOCABS BATCHES (comma lists)."""
import importlib.util, statistics, sys, time
import torch


def load(name, path):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.chain_speculative_sampling_triton


def eager_us(fn, n=60):
    times = []
    for _ in range(n):
        start = time.perf_counter_ns()
        fn()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        times.append((time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / 1000)
    return statistics.median(times)


def replay_us(replay, n=60):
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    start = time.perf_counter_ns()
    for _ in range(n):
        replay()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return (time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / n / 1000


samplers = {
    "main": load("rs_main", sys.argv[1]),
    "pr": load("rs_pr", "python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/reject_sampling.py"),
}
slots, steps = 6, 5
for vocab in map(int, sys.argv[2].split(",")):
    for batch in map(int, sys.argv[3].split(",")):
        torch.manual_seed(2026)
        p = (torch.randn(batch, slots, vocab, device="cuda") * 3).softmax(-1)
        noise = (torch.randn(batch, steps, vocab, device="cuda") * 3).softmax(-1)
        q = (0.7 * p[:, :steps] + 0.3 * noise).contiguous()
        cand = torch.zeros(batch, slots, dtype=torch.long, device="cuda")
        cand[:, 1:] = torch.multinomial(q.flatten(0, 1), 1).view(batch, steps)
        idx = torch.arange(batch * slots, device="cuda").view(batch, slots)
        pred = torch.empty(batch * slots, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
        acc = torch.empty_like(idx, dtype=torch.int32)
        num = torch.empty(batch, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
        coins, final = torch.rand(batch, slots, device="cuda"), torch.rand(batch, device="cuda")
        for block in (False, True):
            eager, graph = {k: [] for k in samplers}, {k: [] for k in samplers}
            calls, graphs = {}, {}
            for name, sampler in samplers.items():
                calls[name] = lambda s=sampler: s(
                    pred, acc, num, cand, idx, None, None, coins, final, p, q, 1.0, 1.0, True,
                    block_verification=block,
                )
                calls[name]()
                graphs[name] = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
                with torch.cuda.graph(graphs[name]):
                    calls[name]()
            for round_id in range(9):
                for name in samplers if round_id % 2 == 0 else reversed(list(samplers)):
                    eager_us(calls[name], 10)
                    eager[name].append(eager_us(calls[name]))
                    replay_us(graphs[name].replay, 10)
                    graph[name].append(replay_us(graphs[name].replay))
            med = lambda x: round(statistics.median(x), 2)
            print(vocab, batch, "block" if block else "token",
                  "eager", med(eager["main"]), med(eager["pr"]),
                  "graph", med(graph["main"]), med(graph["pr"]), flush=True)
```

</details>

I validated `18a42c8f56` on B200 with the sampler, DSpark and EAGLE tests and NEXTN serving. I did not verify ROCm, MUSA, UNO serving, multi-layer EAGLE, or GLM-5.3-Flash at this head.

Deliberate limits:

- Eager time exceeds `main` at some sizes from 32,001 to 65,536.
- From 16,385 to 32,767, sizes not divisible by 16 compile in 8 to 10 s, against about 2 s. Up to batch 48, graph time reaches 1.33x of `main` at 32,001.
- Above the default of 48 requests, token-wise time at 32,001 reaches 3.23x of `main` in eager mode and 3.73x in graph mode.

These limits are deliberate. Do not add code for them without a real input that reaches the case.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

[Your team has set up Codex to review pull requests in this repo](https://chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/settings/general). Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review" or "@codex security review". Codex reacts with 👀 while any review is running, comments if it has suggestions, and reacts with 👍 once all reviews finish with no findings.

Fixed the sparse final draw in [a7f21b74aa](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/a7f21b74aabf34b332159f00fccfde52bd7c1c30). I replayed the same probabilities and coins on a B200 in token-wise and block verification:

| Input after rejection | Previous head `57301d4eed` | This head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sparse CDF at 0.5 | 16384 (zero mass) | 16391 (mass 0.49999994) |
| Only token 126 has residual mass; the cutoff rounds to the total | 128 (zero mass) | 126 |
| Empty residual, vocabulary size 129 | 128 | 128 |

The [regressions](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a7f21b74aabf34b332159f00fccfde52bd7c1c30/test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_block_verification.py#L138-L181) fail against the previous head. I ran the registered module on the fix, including the DFLASH path, with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 and sglang-kernel 0.4.10.

To reproduce the kernel comparison from this checkout:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_block_verification.py
git show 181380682b50f4606d1a09df3cbbbfc21de931e3:python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/reject_sampling.py > /tmp/sglang-main-reject-sampling.py
python benchmark/kernels/bench_block_verification.py --baseline-file /tmp/sglang-main-reject-sampling.py --steps 4 --vocab 154880 --batches 4 --warmup 50 --measurement 150 --repeats 5
```

The checked-in benchmark measured **100.66 to 40.67 µs** for token-wise verification and **95.91 to 40.92 µs** for block verification. The PR description gives the separate warm CUDA graph comparison, including small vocabularies. These are sampler timings; I did not run a model server or measure model accuracy on this head.

Could someone with CI access start the base checks on this head? The [upstream gate](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41242493410/job/124659161263) is waiting for the `run-ci` label.

Fixed the sparse final draw in [a7f21b74aa](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/a7f21b74aabf34b332159f00fccfde52bd7c1c30). I replayed the same probabilities and coins on a B200 in token-wise and block verification:

| Input after rejection | Previous head `57301d4eed` | This head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sparse CDF at 0.5 | 16384 (zero mass) | 16391 (mass 0.49999994) |
| Only token 126 has residual mass; the cutoff rounds to the total | 128 (zero mass) | 126 |
| Empty residual, vocabulary size 129 | 128 | 128 |

The [regressions](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/a7f21b74aabf34b332159f00fccfde52bd7c1c30/test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_block_verification.py#L138-L181) fail against the previous head. I ran the registered module on the fix, including the DFLASH path, with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 and sglang-kernel 0.4.10.

To reproduce the kernel comparison from this checkout:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_block_verification.py
git show 181380682b50f4606d1a09df3cbbbfc21de931e3:python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/reject_sampling.py > /tmp/sglang-main-reject-sampling.py
python benchmark/kernels/bench_block_verification.py --baseline-file /tmp/sglang-main-reject-sampling.py --steps 4 --vocab 154880 --batches 4 --warmup 50 --measurement 150 --repeats 5
```

The checked-in benchmark measured **100.66 to 40.67 µs** for token-wise verification and **95.91 to 40.92 µs** for block verification. The PR description gives the separate warm CUDA graph comparison, including small vocabularies. These are sampler timings; I did not run a model server or measure model accuracy on this head.

Could someone with CI access start the base checks on this head? The [upstream gate](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41242493410/job/124659161263) is waiting for the `run-ci` label.
